La Macarena serves as a base for exploring Caño Cristales and the surrounding river landscapes. This is where the overland and boat portions of the journey begin: the group learns about local rules for visiting protected natural areas before setting off along the chosen route. The town is closely connected to the region's natural environment and the work of local guides.

Other places to explore nearby include Caño Cristalitos, Caño Piedra, and Río Bajo Losada. A visit is enriched by local music and regional cuisine. La Macarena offers an encounter between remarkable natural routes and the everyday lives of the residents who welcome travelers.

Viewing the exterior and visiting the interior are separate experiences; access to the building must be confirmed in advance.

La Paz was founded in 1548 under the name La Ciudad de Nuestra Señora de La Paz. The city lies at an altitude of 3,660 meters above sea level. The historic center and San Francisco Square are situated in the lowest part of the valley. From here, brick- and cobblestone-paved streets spread out in different directions, climbing steeply uphill and giving the city its distinctive atmosphere. La Paz is Bolivia's de facto capital and the world's highest-altitude "capital."

The heart of the old city is Murillo Square, surrounded by old colonial-style mansions and numerous churches. The main cathedral, built in the neoclassical style, stands out in marked contrast to the surrounding traditional churches. The broad Prado Avenue is particularly beautiful. Here, tall buildings stand alongside hotels, shops, and restaurants. In the northern part of the avenue lies San Francisco Square, from which indigenous neighborhoods climb the hillsides. Be sure to visit the world's only "Witches' Market," where you can buy a variety of amulets and silver jewelry. And if you enjoy browsing souvenir shops while stopping for a cup of coffee, Sagárnaga Street awaits you.

Another interesting sight is the world's highest-altitude prison, in San Pedro, a traditional district of the city. La Paz is rich in museums, where you can explore the history of Inca civilization. Nightlife enthusiasts will find many restaurants and discos, although the best restaurants and nightclubs, by local standards, are in Sopocachi. About 10 km from the city lies the famous Valle de la Luna ("Moon Valley"), a labyrinth of rocky towers, miniature canyons, and picturesque rock formations.

La Paz Waterfalls are located on the river of the same name in Costa Rica. In La Paz Waterfall Gardens nature park, trails wind through humid forest and lead to five waterfalls. Steps and viewpoints let visitors see the cascades from different angles, follow the flow of the water, and observe vegetation along the riverbanks.

The nature park also features animal and plant exhibits, including a hummingbird gallery, a bird garden, a butterfly farm, and a frog exhibit. Exploring La Paz combines a forest walk with opportunities to observe Costa Rica's wildlife. The site is often included in journeys between San José, Poás Volcano, and the Arenal area.

The market is located in the old part of the city and is included in sightseeing routes. It is a pleasant place to browse stalls and hear stories about local customs. Ask vendors for permission before photographing them; the length of the visit depends on the excursion program. The cover image shows a square in the historic center of La Paz.
